enzyme_name: no enzyme as written; nearest real catalyst is Artemisia annua aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 (ALDH1), which oxidises (11R)-dihydroartemisinic aldehyde to dihydroartemisinic acid
organism_context: Artemisia annua glandular trichomes (plant ALDH family enzyme of the artemisinin pathway)
rationale: This is MetaCyc's class-level reaction ALDEHYDE-DEHYDROGENASE-NADORNOP+-RXN expanded combinatorially, so the substrate (11R)-dihydroartemisinic aldehyde (C15H24O, a cyclic sesquiterpenoid) is paired with the unrelated straight-chain fatty acid Pentadecylic acid (C15H29O2-) and the equation is also one hydrogen short - no single protein catalyses it as written. The enzyme that performs the intended aldehyde oxidation, A. annua ALDH1, is a standalone single-activity NAD+ aldehyde dehydrogenase used as a one-step pathway enzyme in every heterologous reconstruction; no second catalytic domain has been reported for it.
direction_note: ModelSEED's '<' would make this an NAD(P)H-driven reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde, which no NAD(P)+ aldehyde dehydrogenase does (acid reduction needs an activated acyl group or an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase); the large positive dG that drove the '<' call is an artifact of the mis-paired product, because oxidation of an aldehyde to its own carboxylate is strongly exergonic and mechanistically irreversible.

enzyme_name: no enzyme as written; nearest real activity is the soluble NAD+-dependent abietadienal (diterpene aldehyde) dehydrogenase of conifer diterpene resin acid biosynthesis
organism_context: conifers - soluble ALDH activity demonstrated in Abies grandis and Pinus contorta stem extracts; in Pinus taeda the same C18 oxidation is instead run by the P450 CYP720B1/PtAO
rationale: Combinatorial expansion of MetaCyc's class-level ALDH reaction has paired the conifer diterpene aldehyde Abietal (C20H30O, tricyclic) with the unrelated straight-chain C20 fatty acid 8,11,14-Icosatrienoate (C20H33O2-), and the equation is one hydrogen short, so no protein catalyses it as written. The nearest genuine catalyst, the soluble NAD+-dependent abietadienal dehydrogenase of Abies grandis, was only ever demonstrated as an activity in cell-free extracts and never cloned, while in pine the same net oxidation is carried out by the multisubstrate P450 CYP720B1 (consecutive oxidations at one active site, not a fused bifunctional enzyme), so the domain architecture of the actual catalyst cannot be settled.
direction_note: ModelSEED's '<' would make this an NAD(P)H-driven reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde, which no NAD(P)+ aldehyde dehydrogenase does (acid reduction needs an activated acyl group or an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase); the large positive dG that drove the '<' call is an artifact of the mis-paired product, because oxidation of an aldehyde to its own carboxylate is strongly exergonic and mechanistically irreversible. The conifer alternative (CYP720B1) is an O2/NADPH-dependent monooxygenase that is likewise strictly oxidative.

direction_note: ModelSEED's '<' would make this an NAD(P)H-driven reduction of a carboxylate back to an aldehyde, which no NAD(P)+ aldehyde dehydrogenase does (acid reduction needs an activated acyl group or an ATP-dependent carboxylic acid reductase); the large positive dG that drove the '<' call is an artifact of the mis-paired product, because oxidation of an aldehyde to its own carboxylate is strongly exergonic and mechanistically irreversible. The conifer alternative (CYP720B1) is an O2/NADPH-dependent monooxygenase that is likewise strictly oxidative.
